title: Onboard audit: hypothesis-driven regression — continuous batching + paged-KV + flash-attn
body:
Purpose:
This audit captures a focused regression investigation after merging three runtime changes that interact nonlinearly: 1) flash-attn v2 kernel substitution, 2) paged-KV page-size refactor + warmup optimization, and 3) a new continuous-batching scheduler (contbatch-v3). The goal is to document observed diffs on our onboarding eval suite, list reproducible failures, propose root-cause hypotheses, and recommend short-term mitigations for customer-facing Dedicated clusters.

Quick summary (tl;dr):
- Overall token quality (avg BLEU/ROUGE proxies for the onboarding promptset) is stable on most tasks, but we see systematic score drops on long-context summarization and multi-turn reranking tests.
- Latency P95 increased for a subset of workloads exhibiting microburst suffixes when contbatch merges variable-length requests into a single kernel invocation. Median latency unchanged.
- Memory/KV: paged-KV warmup change introduced a transient mismatch where initial KV reads return page-misaligned entries for sequences that begin with high prefix reuse. This correlates with degraded rerank score orderings.
- Flash-attn substitution introduces occasional token-weight perturbations in attention maps for very long sequences (>8k) producing minor factual drift in narrow QA prompts.

Experimental setup:
- Hardware: Dedicated GPU pool (A100-same fleet) mirrored across two shadow nodes: baseline (runtime v2026-07-28) vs candidate (runtime v2026-08-02 with contbatch-v3, paged-kv-refactor, flash-attn-v2).
- Models: rwd-7b-v1 (onboard), rwd-13b-v2 (onboard smoke), and an evaluation rwd-rerank-3b.
- Prompt sets: onboarding-longsumm (20 prompts, average 6k tokens), onboarding-dialogue-rerank (50 multi-turn sessions, 3–12 turns), microseq-halluc (40 targeted QA checks).
- Measurement windows: 2000 requests sampled per promptset per node. Metrics aggregated per-prompt and then averaged.

Key metric diffs (baseline -> candidate):
- onboarding-longsumm: ROUGE-L mean -3.7 points, BLEU-like proxy -2.1 points, perplexity +0.8.
- onboarding-dialogue-rerank: pairwise rerank accuracy -6.4% absolute (candidate worse).
- microseq-halluc: hallucination rate +1.1% (small signal, concentrated in long context QA).
- Latency: p50 +0ms, p95 +42ms median across prompts with bursty lengths; p99 +120ms in worst-case merged batches.
- Memory page faults: transient increase of +14% during first 2 tokens of long contexts (paging warmup).

Representative failure examples (verbatim excerpts):
- Prompt: "Summarize the following 9k-token call transcript and extract action items."
  Baseline summary: concise list of 6 action items with correct actor attribution.
  Candidate summary: omitted actor attribution for items 2 and 4; merged two action items into one sentence (loss of granularity).

- Rerank session (3-turn dialog): gold ordering [A, B, C]; baseline ranked [A, B, C]; candidate produced [B, A, C] with A demoted. Manual inspection shows small score compression between A and B in candidate (delta reduced from 0.42 -> 0.06).

Investigation notes and evidence: 
1) Contbatch merging behavior
- Observation: The new scheduler aggressively combines incoming variable-length requests into a single batched kernel invocation. When the batch contains both very long (>=6k) and short (<256) sequences, the internal sequence-packing step zeros-pad and then reclaims KV pages differently than baseline.
- Hypothesis: Packing order + contbatch kernel path causes relative attention normalization differences for long sequences because flash-attn v2 expects non-interleaved memory layout.
- Evidence: When we replay the candidate runtime with a forced no-merge flag (contbatch disabled), rerank accuracy returns to within 1% of baseline on the same traffic trace.

2) Paged-KV warmup mismatch
- Observation: paged-KV refactor moves from eager prefetch to demand-driven prefetch with a larger page stride. During the first few tokens of very long prefixes (common in onboarding-longsumm), reads hit an uninitialized page state that we patch with zeros leading to subtle token drift.
- Hypothesis: The combination of demand-prefetch + contbatch merging allows one request to observe a page before it's been warmed by prior requests in the same merged invocation, because the merged packing schedules the warmup out of order.
- Evidence: Heap traces show page-read timestamps for candidate are >20ms later compared to baseline for the same sequence; enabling prefetch-for-merge toggles back to baseline quality.

3) Flash-attn kernel numeric micro-diffs
- Observation: Substitution to flash-attn-v2 (optimized kernels) yields small float error accumulation over very deep attention stacks (long contexts) resulting in reweighted attention concentration on recent tokens.
- Hypothesis: Different reduction ordering in the new kernel changes softmax normalization by ~1e-4 per head, compounding over 64 layers for rwd-13b leads to measurable output drift on edge QA.
- Evidence: Deterministic float-diff traces generated from instrumented forward passes show headwise softmax L2 differences consistent with the observed downstream perplexity uptick.

Repro steps (minimal):
- Reproduce rerank regression locally: run evaluation harness with the candidate runtime and the same traffic trace. Re-run with env var REDWOOD_CONTBATCH_MERGE=0 to confirm.
- Reproduce paged-KV warmup: run longsumm prompt with page-size set to original stride; compare first-token page-read histogram.
- Reproduce flash-attn diffs: run single-sequence deterministic forward with float32 and compare attention softmax maps between kernels.

Short-term mitigations (recommended):
- Rollback contbatch aggressive merging for Dedicated onboarding nodes (toggle contbatch merge to conservative heuristics) until contbatch path is hardened.
- Re-enable eager prefetch for paged-KV for sequences with expected prefix-reuse > 60%. Add a preflight warmup for merged batches.
- Add a numerical-compat validation check into the kernel CI that runs 50 long-context samples and asserts headwise softmax L2 within threshold.

Longer-term actions / owners:
- contbatch: adjust packing algorithm to preserve per-request warmup ordering and add a merge-safety flag (owner: Jordi Morales, ETA: 2w).
- paged-kv: add speculative prefetch and a consistency check that validates read-after-warm-page timestamps (owner: Priya Desai, ETA: 3w).
- flash-attn: upstream kernel maintainers to add stable reduction ordering option; add a runtime fallback to baseline attn kernel when numeric diff > threshold for long contexts (owner: Ben Carter, ETA: 4w).
- Monitoring: productize an onboarding-specific alert that triggers when rerank-accuracy drops >4% or longsumm-ROUGE drops >2 points in a 1h window (owner: observability team).

Open questions and experiments to run next:
- Can we design a contbatch packing heuristic that groups by sequence-length quantile to avoid interleaving long + short sequences? Quick experiment: quantile bucketing reduced p95 microbursts in local tests.
- What is the cost tradeoff of re-enabling eager prefetch for paged-KV at scale? Need cost sim from infra.
- Is there a simpler numerical stabilization (layernorm/softmax reorder) we can apply in runtime to reduce accumulation without losing perf?

Action items (immediate):
- [Aisha] Push contbatch conservative toggle to Dedicated staging, set nightly AB test.
- [Jordi] Prototype packing-by-quantile and report perf/latency tradeoffs within 5 days.
- [Priya] Add page-prefetch-for-merge flag and a microbenchmark for page-read timing.
- [Ben] Implement CI softmax-L2 check and add a canary job that runs nightly on 10 long-context samples.

Appendix: quick log snippets and traces (abbreviated)
- Candidate batch trace: merge_id=0x7a9f, sequences=[s1:9400,tok, s2:120,tok, s3:3200,tok] pack_order=[s2,s3,s1] page_reads=[t=5ms->page12, t=30ms->page13, t=62ms->page40]
- Baseline batch trace: merge_id=0x6b2c pack_order=[s1,s3,s2] page_reads=[t=2ms->page12, t=18ms->page13, t=25ms->page40]

Notes about doc provenance:
- This is a working audit from the applied-ml onboarding squad. Traces and reproductions saved in linked artifacts. The recommended short-term mitigations are intentionally conservative to reduce customer impact while we iterate on fixes.

End of audit.
